newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major developments in the air cargo industry in the week April 18-25, 1997.
**APRIL 18**

PARIS - A Reuters survey showed the scrapping of the fuel surcharge in the past few days and generally satisfactory market conditions has given several airlines scope to plan rates increases in May from France to the Americas.
WARSAW - LOT said it plans to expand and mulls floating a minority stake or issuing convertible bonds
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa confirmed it would release on May 14 its plans for cooperation with its four main airline partners.
* Eurowings said it was seeing rising airfreight demand for Poland due to truck congestion at the German-Polish border.
* Eurowings said it aims to increase freighter charter business in 1997.

ZURICH - SAirGroup said it had taken precautionary provisions of 300 million Swiss francs in its 1996 accounts to cover various possible future measures, including further measures at Belgian partner Sabena.
* SairGroup said it was on target in its business so far this year, but company executives declined to give a specific forecast for 1997.
*SAirGroup said Swissair's flight operations made a loss of around 120 million Swiss francs in 1996, but it hoped to make significant progress this year in cutting this deficit.
* Swissair said it was cutting its fares to the United States by 15 to 20 percent from April 19 to match fares by its competitors.
*SAirGroup said the completion of an open sky and anti-trust agreement between the United States and Singapore should have a positive impact on the partnership between Singapore Airlines and Swissair
*SAirGroup predicted turbulent European skies and said provisions of 300 million Swiss francs in 1996 should help it survive the coming industry shakeout.
AMSTERDAM - The European Air Cargo Association has formally disbanded itself after two years of existence, one of its founders, Peter Schoute told Reuters.
* Stan Wraight, vice president sales of KLM Cargo, will leave on May 1, a KLM statement said.
TBILISI - Air British Petroleum and Aviatoplivoservice announced that they have set up a joint venture to supply Tbilisi airport with fuel.
COPENHAGEN - FLS Industries said its UK-based FLS Aerospace unit signed a five year, 160 million crown aircraft maintenance deal with British Caledonian Airways.
FRANKFURT - Flughafen said South Korean carrier Asiana Airlines will start weekly flights between Seoul and Frankfurt from May 29
ROME - Interior Minister Giorgio Napolitano said on Friday that media reports of planned attacks in Italy by Islamic extremists were alarmist.

LONDON - A Reuters survey showed the near total elimination of air cargo fuel surcharges coupled with a general lull in customer demand has cut the cost of airfreight from Britain to most Asia, Australasia and Mideast markets.
FRANKFURT - Air France said Otto Meyer has replaced Helmut Scherret as cargo manager for Germany,
MIAMI - Anchorage International Airport's location has long made it a quick pit stop for aircraft but it is hoping to become a major cargo center.said Morton Plumb the airport's director.
LONDON - AB Airlines said it plans to start a twice-daily London Gatwick-Lisbon scheduled passenger BAC 1-11 service from May and will be selling cargo space at the low rate end of the market.
**April 20**

PARIS - Jacques Maillot, chairman of Nouvelles Frontieres, said he was still interested in buying French airline AOM to strengthen the travel company's market position and to get more slots at Orly airport in Paris.
PHOENIX - Air cargo executives said regulatory hurdles in Asia restrict cargo carriers from transporting goods between two foreign nations, inflate prices and limit service.
*Airline experts said mega-alliances involving several international airlines will dominate the future of the airline industry, leaving "unmarried" carriers to flounder
**April 21**
AUCKLAND - Auckland International Airport's two main shareholders have appointed Merrill Lynch to review the company's capital structure, the New Zealand Herald reported.
MANAMA - Gulf Air plans to axe at least 400 more jobs this year to cut costs, Bahrain's Gulf Daily News reported.
LONDON - All BA European flights from London's Gatwick airport were stopped until 1300 GMT following a security alert, a spokeswoman for the airport said
* BA Said it had pushed back by two hours to 1500 GMT its resumption of flights from London's Gatwick airport.
DUBAI - A Reuters survey showed that after a slow start to the year Dubai's air cargo market has turned the corner, with business picking up strongly and rates moving up in tandem.
HONG KONG - A.company official said Hainan Airlines has tentatively priced its initial public offering of 71 million B shares at between 3.5 and four yuan.
SEOUL - Emery said it has formed a wholly-owned company, Emery Worldwide Korea Company Ltd, offering air and ocean freight services.
ROME - Cargo traffic handled through Genoa fell 7.3 percent in first quarter 1997 compared to the same 1996 period, the airport authority said.

TOKYO - The Japanese government proposed unlimited aviation rights for two Japanese and two U.S. carriers, and an easing of rules on "beyond rights" for U.S. airlines, a Japanese government source reported.
PARIS - Talks resumed between unions, who have now been on strike for 13 days, and management at British Airways' French airlines Air Liberte and TAT the French daily Le Monde reported

MOSCOW - A Reuters survey showed Moscow forwarders were anxiously awaiting a cancellation of a recent customs ban on transit cargo at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport whilst air cargo rates stayed stable.
STAMFORD - Hexcel Corp said it entered into an agreement to acquire selected assets and businesses of Fiberite Inc for about $300 million in cash and certain assumed liabilities.
WASHINGTON - Southwest Airlines for the second year in a row, was rated the top U.S. carrier, according to the annual Airline Quality Ratings put out by two Midwest universities.
BUDAPEST - Lufthansa said it planned to fly a Boeing B747-200F cargo airplane into Budapest in early May to deliver roughly 30 tonnes of raw material from India for Hungary's pharmaceutical industry.
ST. LOUIS - TWA said it expected its first-quarter loss and finished the period "ahead of plan," and it expects "unusual" costs to decline in the second and third quarters.

ATLANTA - ASA Holdings and Atlantic Southeast Airlines said that it had executed a purchase agreement with Bombardier Inc to acquire 30 Canadair Regional Jet aircraft with options for an additional 60 aircraft.
LONDON - Avianca said it will aim at carrying high-yield, mainly low volume cargo traffic on its new twice-weekly London Heathrow-Bogota passenger services, due to start on May 2.
NEW YORK - Airborne Express said it would open a new international service centre and gateway in Elizabeth, New Jersey on June 1.
PARIS - Air France reported a 3.4 percent increase in cargo traffic in March 1997, with 452.5 million freight tonne kilometres.
HONG KONG - Dragonair is to launch its 16th regional service to mainland China with an inaugural flight to Chongqing on April 23, senior airline officials said.
MOSCOW - A Russian airline has won an order to export elephants to Uganda later this year, a company official said on Monday.
BRUSSELS - Sabena said it would start flying directly from Brussels to Beirut from May 18.

HONG KONG - Direct air links between China and Taiwan could happen at any time but would not have a big impact on Hong Kong Dragon Airlnnes, said Augustus Tang, general manager of planning and international affairs.
KEY BISCAYNE - FedEx expects to create a Latin American hub in Miami within the next two years and add a hub in Latin America later, a top FedEx official said
PARIS - Eurocopter said it made a net consolidated loss of between 350 and 400 million francs in 1996 and abandoned plans to cut 300 jobs in 1998.
OTTAWA - Canadian industry ministry said that it is investing C$3.25 million in Fleet Industries Corp to support an 11-year project to design and build aircraft wing components.
DUBAI - Emirates Airline's air freight division, Emirates Sky Cargo, said it registered a 23 percent increase in tonnage uplifted in the year to end-March 1997 over the previous year.
NEW YORK - The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey might delay the sale of $932 million of airport improvement bonds until next week, an official with lead underwriter Lehman Brothers said
WASHINGTON - The Federal Aviation Administration awarded an air traffic control modernization contract to a unit of General Motors that could be worth up to $100 million.
MINNEAPOLIS - Northwest Airlines and Garuda said they signed a commercial cooperation agreement to offer enhanced benefits for travel between the United States and Indonesia.

NEW YORK - U.S. Airways will begin cutting unprofitable routes and may cancel a pending 400-aircraft order if it does not have a competitive cost structure in place by September 30, the pilots union said.
CHICAGO - DHL said it has opened new facilities in Chicago and Miami this week to cope with expanding demand for both express and logistics products.
HOUSTON - Continental Airlines said it dropped its cargo fuel surcharge on all routes with effect Monday April 21.
**APRIL 22**
SINGAPORE - A borderless system for customs control in the seven member states of the Association of Southeast aAsian Nations would be a major boost for cargo shippers, an industry executive said
HARARE - Zimbabwe expects to earn Z$1.5 billion from horticulture exports in the marketing season ending in June, up from Z$997.4 million last year, an industry official said on Tuesday.
HONG KONG - The Hong Kong Association of Freight Forwarding Agents will elect a new chairman at its annual general meeting on April 29 following the resignation of its current chairman, Sam Chung
HELSINKI - Finnair said it would expand its co-operation with Delta Air Lines by introducing a new code share flight between Helsinki and San Francisco.
FRANKFURT - Lufthansa said it had signed a code-sharing agreement with Thai Airways to cover destinations in Bangladesh, Brunei, Laos and Nepal.
BRUSSELS - Thai Airways International has temporarily stopped flying to Brussels, an airline spokesman said.

HONG KONG - Salomon Brothers said the Chinese airline industry's long term growth prospects are among the best in the world and traffic is forecast to grow at 15 to 20 percent annually over the coming years,
* Air Hong Kong will increase its ex-Europe frequencies to nine from the present four times a week in August, said its European general anager, Marcel Buelens.
* Air Hong Kong will drop its cargo fuel surcharge from May 1, said Buelens.
MINNEAPOLIS - Northwest Airlines said the second quarter is expected to be more challenging than the first, with little improvement seen in fuel prices and the yen remaining weak.

KEY BISCAYNE - Florida West International Airlines, an all-cargo airline, has moved into new facilities at Miami International Airport, expanding its warehouse capacity dramatically, its chief executive said.

* All Caribbean airlines in the Caribbean are meeting to try and strike co-operative agreements that could make them more efficient in cargo and passenger operations, a chief executive of one of the airlines said
* United Airlines hopes to strike a pact with its code-share partners that would require all the carriers to agree to certain safety standards, a top officer said
ROME - Transport unions launched the first in a wave of strikes on 22nd April that looks set to hamper travel in Italy over the next two weeks.
PARIS - Four unions representing cockpit crews at airline Air France Europe said they have called a 48-hour strike starting on April 25.

WARSAW - The Polish government decided to proceed with a long-delayed partial privatisation of the national air carrier LOT SA and confirmed that the state would retain a 51-percent stake in the firm after the sell-off.
SOFIA - Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines will start talks with Germany's Bayerische Vereinsbank for the consolidation of the airline's foreign debt, an airline spokesman said
NEW YORK - United Airlines said it expects 1997 to be another record year and sees second quarter earnings slightly above last year.
* Shares of Eagle USA Airfreight dropped 33 percent after its second quarter results failed to meet Wall Street expectations, analysts said.
LONDON - BA World Cargo said it has postponed planned UK-Israel cargo flights for the third time this year and is now looking at mid-June, end-September or even late-1997 as the start-up date.
*BA said that because of pressure on landing and take-off slots, it has begun moving its ex-London cargo flights to Stansted from Gatwick.

MIAMI - AMR Corp chief executive Robert Crandall said the company was ready to move ahead with a new Miami International Airport terminal and has selected veteran aviation management firm Corgan Associates to head its planning and design.
PANAMA CITY - Panamanian airline Aerolineas del Pacifico will make a $10 million bond issue on April 28, a stock exchange spokeswoman said
WASHINGTON - The U.S. and France opened three days of talks toward a free-market "open skies" aviation agreement that would end restrictions on flights between the two countries.
SEATTLE - Boeing plans to add about 10,000 jobs in 1997 in a sharp slowdown from the hiring spree that saw the company add 21,000 positions in 1996, a company spokesman said

PARIS - Two out of five unions representing cockpit crews at British Airways, French airlines TAT and Air Liberte signed an agreements to end a two-week strike and return to work on 23 April, Air Liberte said.
ATLANTA - Delta Air Lines said it filed an application with the U.S. Department of Transportation for authority to fly to Chile.
